speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics. Can you tell me which antibiotic you were prescribed and for how many days? Did your symptoms start immediately after finishing the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Secondary Syphilis (in an 8-year-old, this is extremely unlikely and would require confirmation of maternal exposure or congenital syphilis; however, given the clinical presentation of fever, maculopapular rash starting in flexural areas, and arthralgia post-antibiotics, the most probable diagnosis is actually DRESS syndrome (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms) or Serum Sickness-like reaction, but the rash distribution strongly suggests Disseminated Gonococcal Infection or perhaps a viral exanthem like Parvovirus B19 if the "sinusitis" was viral.
